reviews.comment: This class is the easiest class I've ever taken.  All exams/quizzes were open note and open resource.  There was one quiz per week over one chapter, and 3-4 exams overall.  It was probably just this easy because it was online, so if you see this professor with this online course I definitely recommend taking it for an easy A.

I've taken a similar intro meteorology course elsewhere, and I enjoyed that class much more than this one. Prof was fine/at least maintained clear communication. I recommend just reading the book for lecture material. Graded work consisted of quizzes, couple exams, and discussion assignments. Wouldn't recommend this online course/prof.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really like the prof and enjoyed this class! She is extremely knowledgeable! I was not too interested in the weather before taking this class but I learned a lot and am now interested in it. I thought Prof Brooks was organized. I knew where to find material and it was helpful to go back to her lectures/notes. 3 exams + weekly quizzes.

I don't like weather/atmospheric sciences but this class was very doable and we had a lot of time for each assignment. Exams make up 75% of the grade but they are open note and usually reading the textbook will help with those. The other 25% is quizzes and short discussion posts.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a great professor, even if she is a little disorganized. She makes up for it by allowing easy access to her recordings and slides by adding them to a google drive. She's also very lenient when it comes to grades. Her Quizzes and Exams are easy and a lot of them are open book too. Textbooks are not always required but a little useful.

She has no business teaching an online class. Very bad with technology, and her notes are all over the place and illegible, so it's easy to get lost. She constantly wrote equations & solutions incorrectly during lectures. Double check her notes like your grade depends on it. You're better off reading the book and checking your work with classmates.

Dr. Brooks is nice and cares about her students, but the class felt a bit too easy and I didn't feel like I learned much even though she's very knowledgeable. She got a lot of flak for being disorganized, but it's somewhat understandable since the class was online.

Had her for atmo 446, she doesn't care about her undergrad students, makes no time to meet with us or help with assignments. She just flexes her research the whole time. Sucks are public speaking, she never makes eye contact the entire time and talks to the board. She will writes equations on the board incorrectly all the time.

Professor Brooks is a really nice lady, and wants her students to do well. Her first few exams were kind of difficult, but she gave significant curves on both. On the third exam she gave an extremely detailed review and tests got significantly easier.  She's doesn't really explain much in class, so don't expect to learn much.

Doesn't cancel class for any reason at all. Very vague and talks more about current forecast than about actual ATMO 201 material that we need to learn to take her hard tests. She teaches straight from her slides that she puts online, but gives "written assignments" (counts as quiz grade) in class randomly so you HAVE to go to her boring lectures.

Gives random pop quizzes/written assignments. She is unprepared for class. She spends 30 minutes of the lecture talking about the current forecast, which is stuff that isn't even on the exams. Exams are very hard with weirdly worded questions. She doesn't post grades on Ecampus so you never know where you stand. DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR.
